messages:
alice: heads up — customer acme reporting sustained throughput drop on dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-ded-42'. p50 went from ~40ms to ~220ms over the last 30m, and 429s are spiking. ticket #ACME-1024. anyone oncall?
ben: oncall here, looking. which model and route? any recent config changes?
alice: model rwd-3.1-quant, route /v1/generate. no recent deploys from our side. metrics show a huge fraction of tiny batches (1-3 requests) — QPS high but avg tokens per request very low.
carla: pulling batcher logs for pool ded-eu-42 now. early signal: continuous_batcher is prefill-dominant, packer emitting a lot of microbatches. log sample: \"[WARN] packer: tiny_batch_rate=0.82 avg_tokens_per_batch=12 scheduler_quantum=8 pack_wait_ms=2\"
dave: that scheduler_quantum=8 + aggressive prefill means packer will prefer low-latency shallow packs for short prompts. with short inputs this can blow throughput — lots of overhead and KV cache churn.
alice: customer says requests are very short ("hi", "ok") and QPS is bursty. they started after switching to dedicated capacity two days ago.
carla: config snippet for the pool:
```
continuous_batcher:
  enabled: true
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_size: 16
  scheduler_quantum: 8
  prefill_policy: aggressive
  pack_wait_ms: 2
```
carla: suggestion: either increase max_batch_tokens and pack_wait_ms to allow larger packs, or reduce prefill aggressiveness so packer waits a bit longer to pack multiple requests.
ben: can we repro with a load script? asking customer for a replay but we should repro in staging first. propose: 500 qps of 1-2 token prompts with concurrency ~50.
dave: repro curl loop to run in staging:
```sh
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -sS -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.com/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3.1-quant","input":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
done
wait
```
alice: ran that in our staging cluster. observed tiny_batch_rate ~0.79, p50 180ms, and a handful of 429s once pool CPU jittered. packing histogram shows 60% of batches size<=2.
carla: quick mitigation I can push: set scheduler_quantum: 16, max_batch_tokens: 8192, pack_wait_ms: 8 for pool ded-eu-42 and enable pack_coalesce=true. will canary on 1 node.
autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler: attempted scale-up for pool ded-eu-42 but failed: quota_exceeded (quota_lock). request_id=az-77.
dave: ah — quota blocked the autoscaler, so even if packer wanted to pause it couldn't rely on autoscale headroom. eng-sre please check pool quota. @eng-sre
eng-sre: checking now, bumping quota for ded-eu-42 by +2 nodes. should be propagated in ~1m.
autoscaler-bot: Autoscaler: quota increased. adding 2 nodes to ded-eu-42. add_node actions initiated.
carla: canary patch applied to 1 node (scheduler_quantum=16, pack_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=8192). observing metrics: tiny_batch_rate dropped to 0.28, avg_tokens_per_batch rose to 56, p50 latency back to ~45ms.
abtest: support-bot: customer ACME notified via ticket #ACME-1024. they confirmed lower error rate in last 10m.
alice: customer confirmed: errors gone, throughput back to expected. planning a postmortem and defaulting new pool profile for short-input workloads.
ben: action items: 1) change default prefill_policy for new dedicated pools that primarily serve short prompts; 2) add an autoscale quota alert so quota_exceeded blocks surface earlier; 3) document recommended scheduler_quantum/max_batch_tokens for short-prompt QPS.
dave: agree. I'll follow up with a small runbook and a config template.
carla: closing alert in monitoring, adding packer metrics to the pool dashboard. :white_check_mark:
alice: thanks all :thumbsup:
